artifacts.name: Lunar Roving Vehicle (LRV)
artifacts.geological_context: Taurus-Littrow Valley floor regolith deposit adjacent to Camelot Crater
artifacts.measured_properties: Conductivity: High (Al alloy / Cu wiring), Depth: 6.5 cm, Magnetic Dipole: Moderate
artifacts.estimated_properties: Total Mass: ~210 kg, Structural Integrity: 88%, Soil Compaction: Low
artifacts.purpose: Electric four-wheel rover to expand astronaut mobility and scientific sample collection
artifacts.status: Stationed permanently on lunar surface at Taurus-Littrow
artifacts.history: Built by Boeing and Delco, the Lunar Roving Vehicle allowed Apollo astronauts to travel up to 35 kilometers from their lunar module, dramatically expanding geological exploration.

artifacts.name: Apollo Lunar Module Descent Stage
artifacts.geological_context: Mare Tranquillitatis basaltic regolith sheet, West Crater ejecta halo
artifacts.measured_properties: Conductivity: Very High (Titanium / Mylar shielding), Depth: 12.0 cm
artifacts.estimated_properties: Residual Propellant: Inert, Footpad Penetration: 7.6 cm into regolith
artifacts.purpose: Rocket-powered descent platform and the base camp for humanity's first lunar landing
artifacts.history: On July 20, 1969, Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin piloted the Eagle to the lunar surface. The descent stage remained on the Moon, serving as the launch pad for the astronauts' return to orbit.
sources: Smithsonian National Air and Space Museum

artifacts.name: Apollo Lunar Surface Experiments Package (ALSEP)
artifacts.geological_context: High-porosity pyroclastic mantling deposit overlying sub-floor basalt
artifacts.measured_properties: Conductivity: High, Thermal Profile: Residual RTG dissipation footprint, Depth: 9.0 cm
artifacts.estimated_properties: Structural Housing: Intact cast Beryllium, Cabling: Partially regolith-cemented
artifacts.purpose: Nuclear-powered geophysical laboratory studying moonquakes, solar wind, and lunar atmosphere
artifacts.status: Deactivated in 1977 after collecting 8 years of seismic and thermal science
artifacts.history: Powered by plutonium-238 radioisotope generators, ALSEP stations transmitted continuous data on lunar seismology and magnetic fields back to scientists on Earth for nearly a decade.

artifacts.name: Ferroan Anorthosite Crustal Clast
artifacts.detection_signature: Weak Magnetic Susceptibility / Metallic Mineral Inclusions
artifacts.geological_context: Deep crustal primordial flotation cumulate excavate from Descartes Formation
artifacts.measured_properties: Plagioclase Feldspar: 96.2%, Density: 2.84 g/cm³, Depth: 28.5 cm
artifacts.estimated_properties: Crystallization Age: ~4.46 Ga (Pre-Nectarian primordial lunar magma ocean)
artifacts.purpose: Decipher the fundamental cooling history and age of the primordial lunar magma ocean
artifacts.status: Pristine sub-surface specimen preserved in vacuum
artifacts.history: Anorthosite is the foundational rock of the bright lunar highlands, formed when plagioclase feldspar crystals floated to the top of the primordial global magma ocean over 4.4 billion years ago.

artifacts.name: Kamacite-Taenite Meteoritic Fragment
artifacts.geological_context: Projectile relict preserved inside a weathered micro-crater rim
artifacts.measured_properties: Nickel: 7.4%, Iron: 92.1%, Widmanstätten lamellae, Depth: 15.2 cm
artifacts.estimated_properties: Impactor Origin: Metallic asteroid core fragment, Impact Velocity: ~14 km/s
artifacts.purpose: Analyze ancient solar system asteroidal differentiation and projectile survival during hypervelocity impacts
artifacts.history: Because the Moon has no atmosphere or liquid water, metallic iron-nickel meteorite fragments remain completely unoxidized for billions of years, offering pristine records of solar system history.

artifacts.name: Pyroclastic Volcanic Glass Spherules
artifacts.dimensions_cm: Core sample tube: 35 cm length x 4 cm diameter
artifacts.geological_context: Deep-mantle fire fountain explosive eruptive deposit at Taurus-Littrow
artifacts.measured_properties: Titanium (TiO2): 8.8%, Iron (FeO): 22.0%, Sulfur volatiles enriched, Depth: 18.0 cm
artifacts.estimated_properties: Eruption Depth: >400 km in lunar mantle, Age: 3.64 Ga
artifacts.purpose: Provide unique window into the volatile content and volatile-rich mantle of the deep lunar interior
artifacts.history: Discovered by geologist Harrison Schmitt at Shorty Crater during Apollo 17, the orange soil consists of microscopic beads of volcanic glass formed in deep lunar fire-fountaining eruptions.

artifacts.name: Jettisoned ALSEP Aluminum Deployment Bracket
artifacts.detection_signature: Distinct High-Frequency Non-Ferrous Aluminum Eddy Signal
artifacts.geological_context: Station 1 deployment perimeter near Central Station cable run
artifacts.measured_properties: Alloy: Anodized Aluminum 6061-T6, Fasteners: Stainless steel 304, Depth: 4.2 cm
artifacts.estimated_properties: Surface Micrometeorite Pitting: 14 pits/cm², Thermal Cycling Fatigue: Moderate
artifacts.purpose: Structural cable harness bracket discarded during ALSEP sub-package separation
artifacts.history: During EVA-1, astronauts deployed the ALSEP station and discarded temporary transport brackets, retaining rings, and cable ties directly onto the regolith.

artifacts.name: Sojourner Rover
artifacts.purpose: Pioneering technology demonstration of the first wheeled rover on the Martian surface
artifacts.status: Mission completed; preserved at Ares Vallis
artifacts.history: The microwave-sized Sojourner rover operated for 83 sols (days) on Mars, traveling 100 meters, taking hundreds of images, and analyzing chemical composition of Martian rocks like 'Barnacle Bill'.

artifacts.name: Opportunity Rover (MER-B)
artifacts.purpose: Search for geological evidence of past liquid water on Mars
artifacts.status: Completed mission in 2018 at Perseverance Valley after 14.5 years
artifacts.history: Planned as a 90-day mission, 'Oppy' drove 45.16 kilometers across Meridiani Planum, discovering hematite spherules ('blueberries') and rock layers formed in ancient standing liquid water.
sources: NASA JPL Mars Exploration Rover Archives

artifacts.name: Ingenuity Mars Helicopter
artifacts.purpose: Technology demonstration of powered, controlled aerodynamic flight on another planet
artifacts.status: Grounded after rotor blade damage; completed 72 historic flights
artifacts.history: Weighing only 1.8 kilograms, Ingenuity made history on April 19, 2021 by achieving the first powered flight in the ultra-thin Martian atmosphere, acting as an aerial scout for Perseverance.
